questions.notes: SLayer's running total (cumsum) needs a time axis, so the supplier revenue rank is turned into a day offset (date_add(base_date, rev_rank, 'day'), base_date = earliest 1997 order date, a declared field) and cumsum runs over that day axis; the rank is read back with date_diff. All inside one multi-stage request, no raw SQL. Tie-break approximated: rank(revenue, desc) has no secondary key (supplier_key asc); no revenue ties among the 10,000 suppliers, so the result is exact here.

ntile always orders ascending, so the decile is ntile(-sum(total_price), n=10), i.e. largest first. Tie-break approximated: ntile cannot take the secondary key (order_key asc); ties in total_price do not change any decile's count, sum, min or max here.
first_order_year is min(orders.order_date) over the customer's lines with no row filter; every order has at least one line, so it equals the customer's earliest order date.

Position 2 by (order_date, order_key) is expressed without row_number: if the customer has 2+ orders on the first date, days = 0, else days = first later order date minus the first date. Exact by construction. The 100000 sentinel is never reached for customers with 2+ orders.

The two manufacturer roles come from two copies of the (order, manufacturer) stage joined on order key with a declared many_to_many cardinality and to_many_handling='associate'. N = distinct 1997 orders seen through lineitem; every order has at least one line, so this equals the number of 1997 orders.
